text.p: British shares opened mixed on Tuesday and dealers said the market was likely to drift through the morning, lacking the guiding hand which Wall Street usually provides and forced to look elsewhere for direction.

The FTSE opened six points lower at 4,331.2 but soon erased its losses and was 2.3 points firmer at 4,340.1 by 0840 GMT. Wall Street was closed on Monday and dealers said the market would seek early inspiration from blue-chip results instead.
"Without any lead from Wall Street it's difficult to see a great deal going on," said the head of sales at a U.S. investment bank in London.
